Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042 ECN-1042 | Page 1 Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042 ECN Number: ECN-1042 Title: Pressure Sensor Replacement (PS-04 → PS-04A) and Operating Pressure Update Effective: Software Revision 3.2 Affected Assembly: Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU) Status: Released 1. Description of Change Effective software revision 3.2, pressure sensor PS-04 is replaced by pressure sensor PS-04A at the HPU discharge line. PS-04A uses an updated signal conditioning circuit and is not a form-fit-function replacement for PS-04; controller firmware must be at revision 3.2 or later to read PS-04A correctly. Alongside the sensor change, the normal HPU discharge pressure setpoint is revised from 180 bar to 200 bar. This is a deliberate process change, not a sensor calibration artifact: the higher setpoint improves press cycle time on Series-7 units manufactured after 2024. PS-04 remains installed and supported on units running software revisions prior to 3.2. Do not install PS-04A on a controller running firmware older than 3.2. 2. Reason for Change Field data showed PS-04's signal drift exceeded tolerance after approximately 18 months of continuous service in high-cycle installations, occasionally triggering nuisance Alarm A19 (Sensor Signal Invalid). PS-04A corrects this drift behavior. 3. Impacted Documentation Operator Manual AEG-OM-700, Maintenance Manual AEG-MM-700, and Component Register AEG-CR-700 have been updated to reflect PS-04A and the 200 bar setpoint. See also ECN-1058 for a related alarm threshold correction.

Engineering Change Notice ECN-1058 ECN-1058 | Page 1 Engineering Change Notice ECN-1058 ECN Number: ECN-1058 Title: Alarm A17 Threshold Reference Correction Effective: Immediately upon publication References: ECN-1042 Status: Released 1. Description of Change The Alarm Reference (AEG-AL-700) description for Alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure Low) referenced the pre-ECN-1042 pressure sensor (PS-04) by name. This notice corrects that reference: Alarm A17's low-pressure condition is evaluated against whichever pressure sensor is active for the installed software revision (PS-04 prior to revision 3.2, PS-04A on revision 3.2 and later). The alarm's threshold logic itself is unchanged by this notice. This is a documentation correction only. No firmware or hardware change is required. 2. Note This notice does not change the operating pressure setpoint established in ECN-1042.

New Operator Orientation — Hydraulic Power Unit Basics
Training Excerpt — Slides 4–6 of the full deck

What is the HPU?
The Hydraulic Power Unit is the heart of the press's hydraulic system.
You'll sometimes hear techs call it the "hydraulic pack" or just "the unit" — same thing.
It pulls fluid from the main reservoir and, on most Line 4/5 configurations, tops up from a smaller Auxiliary Reservoir during peak demand.
Discharge pressure is what the controller watches to decide if the unit is running normally.
Note: “Auxiliary Reservoir” is a Line 4/5-specific configuration detail and is not covered in the standard Operator Manual.

Went out to look at the Line 4 HP unit again, still occasionally throwing the low pressure light even though it doesn't seem to actually be low. Talked to the shift lead, he said it's been doing this on and off since the sensor got swapped out.

Checked the gauge on the local panel and it read about 175 bar during a normal run, not 180 like the manual says it should be. Could be the gauge is a little off, didn't have a calibrated reference on me. Didn't check against the HMI diagnostics screen this time.
Valve (IV-21) looked fine, fully open, no leaks visible. Fluid level looked ok too, maybe a touch low but within the sight glass band.
Alarm history on the panel showed a couple of A17s over the last week, cleared themselves pretty quick each time based on what the operator said — didn't confirm the actual duration.

Recommend someone with a calibrated gauge go check the actual pressure properly, this was just a quick look. Also didn't get a chance to check what software revision the controller is running on this line, might be relevant.
— J. Torres, field service (no date recorded on original notebook page)

Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System — Operator Manual Document AEG-OM-700, Revision 1 (superseded). Applies to software revisions 3.0 and 3.1 only. 1. Overview The Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System provides closed-loop hydraulic pressure regulation for industrial press lines. The system is built around the Hydraulic Power Pack, which supplies pressurized fluid to the press circuit under the supervision of the Aegis Controller. 2. Key Components Reference Component Function Hydraulic Power Pack Hydraulic Power Pack (HPU) Generates and regulates hydraulic pressure IV-21 Isolation Valve 21 Isolates the HPU from the press circuit PS-04 Pressure Sensor 04 Reports HPU discharge pressure to the controller 4. Starting the Hydraulic Power Pack Before starting, verify: Hydraulic fluid level is within the normal band. Isolation valve IV-21 is open. Emergency stop is reset. WARNING: Do not start the unit with the maintenance access panel removed. Turn the POWER selector to ON. Press START. Verify pressure reaches 180 bar . 5. Normal Operating Ranges Normal HPU discharge pressure is 180 bar, as measured by pressure sensor PS-04. 6. Alarms See the Aegis Alarm Reference for alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure Low) and related codes. This legacy export does not reflect ECN-1042 (PS-04 to PS-04A sensor change and pressure setpoint update to 200 bar, effective software revision 3.2) or ECN-1058. Do not use this
document as the sole reference for units running software revision 3.2 or later.

Aegis Series-7 HCS — Maintenance Manual AEG-MM-700 Rev 3 AEG-MM-700 Rev 3 | Page 1 Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System Maintenance Manual Document AEG-MM-700 | Revision 3 1. Scope This manual covers scheduled maintenance, alarm response, and controller behavior for the Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System (HCS). It supplements, and does not replace, the Operator Manual (AEG-OM-700). 3. Controller Reset Conditions Do NOT reset the PLC-03 controller while hydraulic pressure is above 50 bar. The controller reset routine re-initializes valve driver outputs; if the circuit is still pressurized, this can produce a momentary uncommanded actuation of Isolation Valve IV-21. Controller reset is only permitted when pressure, as reported by the active pressure sensor (PS-04 on revisions prior to 3.2, PS-04A on revision 3.2 and later), reads below 50 bar. 4. Alarm A17 Response Alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure Low) may clear on its own within a few seconds if it was triggered by a transient pressure dip during valve transition. If alarm A17 persists for more than 10 seconds, execute Shutdown Procedure 4.7 before investigating further. Do not attempt to clear a persistent A17 by silencing the alarm alone. Shutdown Procedure 4.7: close IV-21, confirm pressure decay, set POWER selector to OFF, tag out per site lockout/tagout procedure, then proceed to Section 6 (Troubleshooting). 6. Troubleshooting: Low Discharge Pressure If the HPU fails to reach normal operating pressure, check the following in order:  Isolation valve IV-21 is closed or partially closed.  Hydraulic fluid level is low.  Pressure sensor (PS-04 / PS-04A) signal is invalid or out of calibration — see Alarm A19 in the Alarm Reference. 7. Component Access The Hydraulic Power Pack (HPU) maintenance access panel is sec

ured by four quarter-turn fasteners. Remove the panel only after the unit has been shut down per Section 4 and pressure has been bled per Section 8. Do not operate the unit with the panel removed. 9. Related Documents Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042 (pressure sensor replacement and setpoint change), ECN-1058 (alarm threshold correction), and the Component Register (AEG-CR-700) should be consulted alongside this manual, as component identifiers and setpoints have changed across software revisions.

Aegis Series-7 HCS — Operator Manual AEG-OM-700 Rev 4 AEG-OM-700 Rev 4 | Page 1 Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System Operator Manual Document AEG-OM-700 | Revision 4 | Applies to software revision 3.2 and later 1. Overview The Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System (HCS) provides closed-loop hydraulic pressure regulation for industrial press lines. The system is built around the Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU), which supplies pressurized fluid to the press circuit under the supervision of the HCS Controller (PLC-03). Throughout Aegis documentation the Hydraulic Power Unit may also be referred to as the Hydraulic Unit or the HP unit, depending on which department produced the document. All three terms refer to the same physical assembly. 2. Key Components Reference Component Function HPU Hydraulic Power Unit Generates and regulates hydraulic pressure IV-21 Isolation Valve 21 Isolates the HPU from the press circuit PS-04A Pressure Sensor 04A Reports HPU discharge pressure to PLC-03 PLC-03 HCS Controller Supervises startup, monitoring, and alarms Note: earlier Aegis units shipped with pressure sensor PS-04. As of software revision 3.2, PS-04 is superseded by PS-04A; see Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042 for details. 4. Operating Procedures 4.3 Starting the Hydraulic Power Unit Before starting, verify:  Hydraulic fluid level is within the normal band on the sight glass.  Isolation valve IV-21 is OPEN.  The emergency stop circuit is RESET. WARNING: Do not start the Hydraulic Power Unit with the maintenance access panel removed. Rotating components inside the HPU housing are exposed when the panel is off. Startup sequence: 1 Turn the POWER selector to ON. 2 Press START. 3 Verify discharge pressure, as reported by PS-04A, reaches 200 bar. This is the normal operating pressu

re for software revision 3.2 and later; see ECN-1042 for the pressure change history. 5. Normal Operating Ranges Normal HPU discharge pressure is 200 bar on software revision 3.2 and later. On revisions prior to 3.2, normal discharge pressure was 180 bar, measured by the original PS-04 sensor. Do not compare live readings against

Aegis Series-7 HCS — Operator Manual AEG-OM-700 Rev 4 AEG-OM-700 Rev 4 | Page 2 the 180 bar figure on a unit running revision 3.2 or later — the setpoint changed along with the sensor replacement. 6. Alarms See the Aegis Alarm Reference (AEG-AL-700) for the full alarm list, including alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure Low), its possible causes, and required operator actions. 7. Controller Reset Do not reset the PLC-03 controller while hydraulic pressure is above 50 bar. Resetting the controller under pressure can cause an uncommanded valve transition. Bleed pressure below 50 bar first, using the manual bleed procedure in Section 8, before performing a controller reset.

Aegis Series-7 HCS — Terminology Glossary
Document AEG-GL-700  |  Revision 2  |  Maintained by Technical Documentation

This glossary lists officially defined terms used across Aegis Series-7 documentation. It is maintained separately from individual manuals and is not guaranteed to be updated at the same time as new Engineering Change Notices. Terms not listed here may still appear in other documents — absence from this glossary does not mean a term is invalid.

Note: this revision of the glossary does not yet include an entry for “HP unit” (used informally in the Operator Manual and training materials) or for the superseded sensor “PS-04”. Readers should not assume a term's absence here means it refers to something different from a listed term — cross-check against the Component Register.

Term | Definition
Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU) | The assembly that generates and regulates hydraulic pressure for the press circuit. See also: Hydraulic Unit.
Hydraulic Unit | Informal short form of Hydraulic Power Unit, used interchangeably in some maintenance documentation.
Isolation Valve (IV-21) | The valve isolating the HPU from the downstream press circuit. Must be open before HPU startup.
PLC-03 | The HCS Controller; supervises startup sequencing, alarm evaluation, and interlocks.
Pressure Sensor 04A (PS-04A) | The HPU discharge pressure transducer used on software revision 3.2 and later.
Alarm | A system-generated notification indicating an out-of-tolerance or fault condition. See the Alarm Reference for the current alarm list.
Setpoint | A configured target value (e.g. normal operating pressure) against which a live measurement is compared.
Engineering Change Notice (ECN) | A controlled document describing an approved change to equipment, software, or documentation.
Software Revision | The version identifier for HCS controller firmware, e.g. 3.2. Governs which components and setpoints are applicable.
